s01-timings.summaryMarkdown: TIME-1 is met. ProcessRunner timestamps every streamed line (stdout and stderr pumps share one Instant); run_plan takes the per-invocation timeline for Libtest invocations and writes artifacts-temp/testkit/<lane>/timings.md. durations() derives deltas between consecutive completion lines from existing parsed output (no libtest flags), resets the baseline at each `running N tests` line so multi-binary runs do not charge build/start-up to the first test, skips ignored tests, marks failures, and attributes tests to the cargo `Running` target. report() gives slowest-first tests with share of the block total, a per-target group table, one block per process, and a build-error/crash/no-match explanation with no table when nothing completed. The new group lane_timings.rs seeds a fixture stream and asserts exact deltas, ordering, shares, the failed marker, the empty message, per-process blocks and a lane run end to end through execute(). I also ran `gpux-testkit lane a --grep tooltip` for real and confirmed the real runner produced a correct timings.md. Non-blocking observations: a run that produces no libtest timeline at all (program missing, runner error, empty selection) leaves a previous timings.md in place, though the run output already reports that failure or empty selection; the `!any && processes.is_empty()` branch in report() is unreachable; lane A is not serial so its durations are bounds, which the report states.

s02-test-profile.summaryMarkdown: OPT-1: whole-profile `[profile.test] opt-level = 1` chosen from measurements (test 10.6 s to 1.1 s, clean build 46 to 83 s, rebuild 6 to 5 s, package overrides and dedicated profile measured and rejected), dev profile untouched, RayX unaffected; every doc figure matches the raw lines. OPT-2: both lane_c_profile tests fail with debug assertions and overflow checks off and pass with them on; group registered in LANE_C_GROUPS.

s03-compare-and-sampling.summaryMarkdown: Repairs verified in source. S03-F1: `Sampling::plan` returns only `compared` over the unchanged script; `compare_with` applies every script step to both windows and draws the layered window after every step, and only the reference draw and `assert_same` follow the plan (stretch of >=16 identical one-pixel steps compares p<4, p>=n-4, p%4==0; a stretch's first and last frames always compared). `assert_composited` is the pre-epic assertion again; `drawn_steps`/`scaled_minimum` are gone. `UNCOVERED_BY_SAMPLED` (78) recomputed independently and matches. Full mode is today's behaviour frame for frame. S03-F2: `lane_c_sampling` seeds covered steps 18, 55, 96, 115 and long scrolls 6 and 13 (fail sampled at that step) and uncovered 20, 61, 100 and the list's last entry (pass sampled, fail full at that step), covering both stretches. CMP-1 and SAMP-3 unchanged and met (lane G's lane C part sets full; the workflow is s05). Hover sampling applies every act to both windows. Note: the saving is modest (about 36 s sampled against 42 s full on Metal), which follows from the literal reading; no criterion sets a threshold.

s04-parallel.summaryMarkdown: PAR-1 is met. The partition, the plan of whole groups per process after one build, one block per process in fixed order, the single summary, failure and empty-run propagation, `--full`, `--list`, narrowed selections and the `--jobs 1` plan are all as specified. The four earlier minor findings are repaired and covered by new tests in `lane_jobs`. Remaining nits, not blocking: the process-runner test does not assert quiet output or timing overlap, and the build-echo test pins the output kind rather than the terminal output.

s05-ci-cadence.summaryMarkdown: Repairs verified at snapshot e9bb7ca9. plan.sh matches CI-1 for every event (hand-run: no labels, ci:lane-a, ci:lane-c, labels, dispatch incl. lane-c-jobs override, schedule, docs-only); `skipped` is now set only when lane-c is selected; ci.yml has the nightly trigger, the nightly concurrency suffix, the full and lane-c-jobs inputs, and the notice goes through env; other jobs, job/step names and the no-push invariant are unchanged; workflow YAML check ok. ci_plan now runs the workflow's own Lane C script under bash -e with a stub cargo (FULL x GREP argv asserted; the gate removal would change the FULL=false argv and fail), missing bash/jq fail rather than skip, and Windows script tests are ignored with a reason. 13 tests pass. Non-blocking note: DISPATCH_LANE_C_JOBS is passed to jq --argjson unvalidated; a non-number fails the plan loudly (dispatch is writer-only).

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Resolved: baseline0.core.log ends `unoptimized + debuginfo` with the original level-0 executable hash (d5ce3793...), gpux recompiled, 5.21 s build / 6 s wall; summary.txt line, table cell (6) and the '5 seconds against 6 at level 0' sentence agree.
Resolved: the dedicated `fastlane` profile is measured (82 s clean, 1.15/1.24 s) in summary.txt and dedicated.build.log, and the doc row and rejection rationale match.

Resolved: noise and monomorphization claims removed or stated as unprofiled, 21% wording matches 8.44/10.63, both runs listed, 83 s next to 46 s for the double build, and the CI pointer now names the epic's last sprint.

Sampled mode shortens the one-pixel scroll instead of sampling it, so the layered window is not 'still drawing every frame it is scrolled through' and the stretch's real last frame is never reached.

Expected (SAMP-1): sampled keeps the whole scripted scroll; the layered window draws every frame of it (tile carry); only the reference draw and comparison are a deterministic subset that always includes the first and last frames of each stretch. Observed: `Sampling::plan` drops the skipped steps from the script for both windows (`steps` holds only kept steps, wheel events are not applied for the rest). The 80-pixel down sweep becomes a 26-pixel sweep and the 40-pixel up sweep 16 (57 of 135 steps); the offsets 26..79 of the sweep (the one whose docstring says it exists to cross every step of a card's shadow over the viewport edges) and the stretch's original last frame are never drawn or compared by any frame, and every later step runs from a different scroll position than in full mode. `lane_c_list_hover` does it the faithful way (every act is applied to both windows, only the reference draw is skipped), so the two suites differ in kind. SAMP-2: `UNCOVERED_BY_SAMPLED` lists only the 23 drawn-but-uncompared plan steps; the 78 script steps that sampled drops are not listed as uncovered and cannot be seeded (the seed is an index into the sampled plan), so a defect at one of them passes a sampled run while the documented 'seeds it does not cover' say nothing about it, and docs/testing.md does not say the sweep is shortened.

Repair: either (a) make the plan apply every script step to both windows and the layered window draw after every one (drawn == script, so `scaled_minimum` is unchanged), and let only the reference draw and `assert_same` follow the subset (first and last of each stretch always, every 3rd or 4th between; hover's `sample_runs` already does this) with the frames-compared tests and the uncovered list updated; or (b) if the cheaper shortened sweep is the intended trade, amend SAMP-1/d-sampling and docs/testing.md to state it plainly (the sweep is shortened, offsets beyond the kept steps and the stretch's original last frame are left to the full and nightly runs), keep the stretch's final offset reachable, and list the dropped script steps as uncovered in the support module and in `lane_c_sampling`.

The coverage lists are asserted against the rule, but only one covered seed (step 18) and one uncovered seed (`UNCOVERED_BY_SAMPLED[0]`, step 17) are seeded end to end, both in the first (downward) stretch; the upward stretch and the other 22 uncovered steps are never run through `compare_with`. Expected: the test that asserts both lists also shows the behaviour for a seed of each stretch, so a drift between `compared` and what `compare_with` actually draws would be caught for the second stretch too. Repair: add a covered and an uncovered seed in the upward stretch (cheap on Metal, the lane keeps every case under a minute) and, if the repair of S03-F1 changes the plan, rebase the seeds on it.

Expected: a failed or slow pre-worker build is as visible as today's lane C run, where cargo's output streams live. Observed: the `prebuild` invocation is `OutputKind::Listing`, which `ProcessRunner` never echoes, and `run_concurrently` in `gpux_testkit.rs` prints only `exited with code N before the workers started; see <log>` on failure. A cold opt-level-1 build prints nothing for minutes, and a compile error is only in the log. Repair: echo the build's output (give the prebuild a streaming output kind, or print `result.output` on failure). Add a test with a fake runner asserting the build output reaches `out` when the build fails. Resolved: the prebuild is now `OutputKind::Libtest`, so `ProcessRunner` echoes it live; a test pins that it is not a `Listing`.

Expected: the concurrent behaviour of the production runner is covered, not only the orchestration. Observed: every `lane_jobs` runner test uses a fake `Runner` that overrides `run_concurrently`, so `ProcessRunner::run_concurrently` (thread per job, quiet output, panicked-thread to failure mapping, result order) has no automated check; running serially, echoing live or losing order would still pass. Real concurrency was shown only by a manual run (205 passed, 26 s against 43 s). Repair: add a test running two short real processes (for example `cargo --version` or a portable program) through `ProcessRunner::run_concurrently`, asserting both results arrive in job order and nothing is echoed. A sleep-based overlap check is optional. Resolved: a test runs real processes through `ProcessRunner::run_concurrently`, asserting result order, per-job timelines and logs, and that an unstartable job fails only its own slot.

Expected (epic constraint: a concurrency level is reported, nothing degrades silently): a `--jobs n` that cannot take effect says so. Observed: `lane a|d|g --jobs 3`, and `lane c --jobs 3 --scene x|--grep y`, run one process and say nothing. `plan_with_jobs` ignores `jobs` outside the full lane C, and `local_gpu` plans lane G's lane C with `lanes::plan` (one process, correct because lane G measures timing) without telling the user. Repair: print one line (for example `lane g: --jobs ignored, runs one process`) when `args.jobs > 1` and the plan has no prebuild, and document in `docs/testing.md` that `--jobs` applies to the full lane C only. Resolved: `lane` prints "--jobs N applies to the full lane c only" for non-C lanes and for a narrowed lane C, `docs/testing.md` says so, and a test covers both lines plus the absence of the line for a full lane C.

Expected: the new group's `--jobs 1` equivalence test can fail. Observed: `one_job_is_exactly_the_plan_the_lane_runs_today` compares `plan(C)` with `plan_with_jobs(C, 1)`, and `plan` is defined as `plan_with_jobs(.., 1)`, so the assertion is always true. The real pin of today's command line is the existing `tests/cli.rs` assertion (about line 269), outside the new group. Repair: in `lane_jobs`, pin the literal single-process command line, or run `lane c --jobs 1` through `execute` with the recording runner and assert exactly one invocation, no build and no `concurrent processes` line. Resolved: a test runs `lane c --jobs 1` through `execute` and pins the literal single cargo command, one invocation, no build and no concurrent-processes line.

Expected: the ci_plan test checks the workflow's mode and jobs wiring so that it fails if lane C's step stops honouring the plan (rules.md: a check must be able to fail). Observed: `lane_cs_step_passes_the_plans_mode_and_jobs_and_keeps_its_names` only does `joined.contains(...)` on text: `"--full"` anywhere and `--jobs "$JOBS"` anywhere. Deleting the gate `[ "$FULL" = true ] &&` (always full, or never full), or inverting it, or letting `--grep` and `--jobs` interplay break, leaves the test green, and the Lane C step's shell logic is never executed; likewise the plan->job output hand-off is checked by substring only. The ci.yml 'parse' is line/substring matching, not YAML (check_workflow_yaml.rb is not part of the test), so an indentation error that moves `FULL`/`JOBS` out of the step `env:` also passes. Repair: extract the `Lane C` step's `run:` block from ci.yml (the text after `run: |` up to `shell:`), run it with `bash -e` and a stub `cargo` first on PATH that records its argv, for FULL=true/false/empty x GREP set/empty, and assert the argv (`--full` only when FULL=true, `--jobs N` only without GREP, `--grep` forwarded). Add one seeded-difference assertion (e.g. the extracted script with the gate removed fails the same assertion) or at least assert the env block of that step (FULL/JOBS/GREP) by step rather than whole job. Keep it Unix-only with the skip reported per CI-PLAN-SKIP-SILENT.

Expected: a prerequisite that is missing is reported skipped with its reason and a run that must cover it asserts it (rules.md: a lane never degrades silently; `GPUX_EXPECT_BACKEND` precedent). Observed: `plan_in` returns None on `cfg!(windows)` or when `bash`/`jq`/`git` is missing and prints one `eprintln!`. libtest captures stderr of passing tests, so the skip is invisible without `--nocapture`, and the 8 plan tests still count as passed (the check's `minimumTests: 8` is met by vacuous passes). On the hosted `test (ubuntu/macos)` jobs a vanished `jq` would silently pass all plan tests while the script is unproven; on Windows (where Git bash and jq are normally present) the plan tests never run at all. Repair: when `CI` (or `GPUX_EXPECT_PLAN_SH`) is set on a non-Windows host, a missing bash/jq/git must fail the test instead of skipping; otherwise mark the skip visibly (e.g. `println!` is also captured, so use a single test that collects and fails/ignores, or document in docs/testing.md that Windows skips by design and make the Windows skip explicit via `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore = "plan.sh needs bash and jq on a Unix host")]` so libtest reports `ignored` with the reason).

Expected: the plan reports the lane C platform it left out when lane C is where the omission matters. Observed: plan.sh computes `skipped` from `platforms` and `warp` only, never from `jobs`, so a docs-only pull request (jobs=[check]) or a `ci:lane-a` label (verified by hand) still prints `lane C skipped on warp (windows-2025): add the ci-os:windows label ...` and the `::notice` annotation, although lane C was not selected at all and nothing was 'skipped'. Repair: only set `skipped` when `lane-c` is in `jobs`; add one assertion to the docs-only test that `skipped` is empty. (The `::notice` text interpolates `${{ steps.plan.outputs.skipped }}` into the script; it is built from constants so it is not injectable today, but passing it through `env:` as the other steps do is the safer shape.)

Observations to settle before s06 closes, not blockers for this sprint's criteria: (a) the concurrency group is `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}` and the nightly now shares `refs/heads/main` with manual dispatches on main; `cancel-in-progress: false` still lets a newly queued run replace an already pending one, so a dispatch queued behind a running nightly (or two dispatches) can drop the other pending run. Consider adding `github.event_name` to the group for `schedule`. (b) `lane_c_jobs` sets ubuntu=2 and macos=2 with no recorded measurement (docs/measurements/lane-c-timings.md does not mention `--jobs`); the task text only fixes Windows at 1. s06 (PAR-2/TIME-2) must record the measured values that justify 2 or reset them to 1. (c) docs/ci.md and the plan's comment are accurate; docs/testing.md is s06's.
